items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: watching MTV, I was watching it last night and some of that stuff is pretty scary where that has — Marilyn Manson and few other things.

ctx.x: When you listen to some of the early Chuck Berry for instance, you almost hear this very interesting conflict because some of the band is still swinging, and Chuck is playing straight eighth notes on his guitar. It’s like adjusting itself.

Okay, they were probably, that was probably a link going there to some of the things that evolved later. I mean people say well how do you distinguish between jazz and rock. Well the music evolved from the other. I mean it was swing. Rock came out of jazz. It came out of rhythm and blues. I remember in high school my buddy and I would ride around late at night after a game or something and head to the diner, and on the radio in the car we used to listen to rhythm and blues. This was in the early or mid-fifties.…
Scary is a pretty good word.
